paragraphs: Yitzchak, the father of Rav Nachman.

In Taanit 21b, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak called himself “a maneh, son of a peras.” Rashi explains that his father was called simply “Yitzchak” because he had not been ordained. Haggahot Ya'avetz, however, explains that the father of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was not wealthy.[^1]

He had a God-fearing wife, as related in Shabbat 156b: Chaldean astrologers told her that her son would be a thief. She therefore took care that her son (Rav Nachman) covered his head, and told him: “Cover your head, so that the fear of Heaven will be upon you.”[^2]

notes.text: A maneh is a monetary unit, and a peras is half a maneh, not a Persian personal name. Rashi on Taanit 21b:6:1 explains the missing title before Yitzchak as indicating that he had not been ordained. Haggahot Ya’avetz’s contrasting explanation about wealth is reported by Hyman.
The fuller account is at Shabbat 156b:6. Its plural אמרי לה כלדאי means that Chaldean astrologers told her; Hyman abbreviates the rest of the story.
